elements.quote: We updated a living systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate the extent of SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools.
elements.reason: The abstract (Background/Methods section) explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review (and meta-analysis).

elements.quote: We updated a living systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate the extent of SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools.
elements.reason: The objective/review question (extent of SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools) is explicitly stated in the abstract.

elements.quote: In this update we modified our inclusion criteria to include: 1) cohort studies; 2) cross-sectional studies that investigated and cross-assessed SARS-COV-2 positivity rates in schools and communities; and 3) pre-post studies.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the main inclusion criteria for study types; exclusions are implied through these specifications.
The abstract does not name the information sources (databases) searched nor report when each source was last searched; this appears only in the full Methods (text_4).

elements.quote: We performed risk of bias evaluation for all included studies using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS).
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the risk of bias assessment method.

elements.quote: We performed a meta-analysis on nine of the 11 cohort studies investigating IAR in schools.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates that results were synthesized via meta-analysis.

elements.quote: we identified 11 cohort studies (1 st update: n = 5; 2 nd update: n = 6) and one cross-sectional study (1 st update: n = 1; 2 nd update: n = 0)
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (12: 11 cohort, 1 cross-sectional) and participant numbers (91 student and 52 staff index cases, 5698 contacts).

elements.quote: Nine cohort studies reported a total of 91 student and 52 staff index cases that exposed 5698 contacts with 101 secondary infections (overall infection attack rate (IAR) = 1.45%, 95% CI = 0.31%-3.26%).
elements.reason: The abstract reports results for the main outcomes (IAR and positivity rates) with numbers of studies and participants.

elements.quote: overall infection attack rate (IAR) = 1.45%, 95% CI = 0.31%-3.26%
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the pooled estimate with its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: Higher IAR were found in students, compared to staff.
elements.reason: When groups are compared, the abstract indicates the direction of effect and which group (students) is favored/higher.

elements.quote: The risk of bias was found to be high for most studies identified, limiting the confidence in results.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes the key limitation of the evidence (high risk of bias).

elements.quote: Emerging evidence suggests the overall IAR and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rate in school settings are low.
elements.reason: The Conclusions section of the abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract does not state the primary source of funding; funding information appears only at the end of the Discussion (text_14).
The abstract does not provide the registry name or registration number; PROSPERO registration (CRD42020192839) is reported only in the Methods/Protocol section (text_3).
No retrieved evidence from the introduction/rationale describes the current state of knowledge or important uncertainties motivating the review.
No retrieved evidence explicitly explains the importance of, or need for, conducting the review in an introduction/rationale section.

elements.quote: Our previous review suggested lower IAR and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rate in students compared to school staff [4], whereas in this update when we combined studies from the second and first update we found higher IAR in students when compared to school staff.
elements.reason: The manuscript is an update and cites the previous review [4], explaining how this update differs; however, this appears in the Discussion rather than a rationale statement in the Introduction, and the need for updating is only implied.
This is a review of SARS-CoV-2 transmission (incidence/prevalence), not a review of intervention effects, so a mechanism of action description does not apply.
The review addresses transmission in schools rather than evaluating a complex intervention, so a logic model is not required.

elements.quote: We updated a living systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate the extent of SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the review objective: to investigate the extent of SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools, with the aim of comparing it to community transmission noted in the conclusions ('to compare it to community transmission').

elements.quote: In this update we modified our inclusion criteria to include: 1) cohort studies; 2) cross-sectional studies that investigated and cross-assessed SARS-COV-2 positivity rates in schools and communities;
elements.reason: The comparison of school vs community transmission is implied (cross-sectional studies comparing positivity rates in schools and communities; conclusions mention comparing school to community transmission), but no explicit PICO-formulated statement of planned comparisons is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: based on updated inclusion and exclusion criteria following the population, exposure, comparison, outcome (PECO) approach... We included children (defined as ≤18 years old) who were attending school, and their close contacts... For study outcomes, we included infections traced to a school index case with a COVID-19 positive test. We updated inclusion criteria of study types to include: 1) Cohort studies... 2) Cross-sectional studies... 3) Pre-post studies
elements.reason: Population, exposure, outcome, eligible study designs, and setting details are explicitly specified using a PECO framework.

elements.quote: We included articles in peer-reviewed journals and pre-prints, and excluded comments, conference abstracts and interviews... with entry date limits from December 2019
elements.reason: Publication status (peer-reviewed and pre-prints) and date limits are specified, but language restrictions are not reported.

The review does not distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported; exclusions described relate to study design/comparison (e.g., cross-sectional studies without community comparison).

elements.quote: We found 11 cohort studies [13-17,24-29] that investigated secondary infection attack (Table 1 and Table 2) and one cross-sectional studies [18] that investigated SARS-CoV-2 positivity compared to community rates (Table 3 and Table 4).
elements.reason: Synthesis groups (cohort studies for IAR meta-analysis, cross-sectional for positivity comparison) are identifiable, but the grouping is not explicitly linked to the comparisons defined in the review objectives.
Notable restrictions (e.g., excluding home-schooled children, schools with fewer than 20 students, household studies) are stated without any rationale.

elements.quote: We searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, ERIC, Embase, WHO COVID-19 database, medRxiv on 26 November 2020 with entry date limits from December 2019
elements.reason: The search date (26 November 2020) is explicitly reported for all listed sources.

elements.quote: We searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, ERIC, Embase, WHO COVID-19 database, medRxiv on 26 November 2020 with entry date limits from December 2019
elements.reason: Database names and coverage start (December 2019) are given, but search interfaces/platforms are not specified.

elements.quote: WHO COVID-19 database, medRxiv on 26 November 2020 with entry date limits from December 2019
elements.reason: The WHO COVID-19 database (a register/repository) and medRxiv are named with date limits, but no separate register searches are described beyond these.
No websites or search engines were reported as searched; no evidence of such sources.
No organisations or manufacturers contacted are reported.
No individuals contacted to identify studies are reported.
No reference list examination is reported.
No citation searching is reported.
No journals or conference proceedings were hand-searched; conference abstracts were explicitly excluded.

elements.quote: We searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, ERIC, Embase, WHO COVID-19 database, medRxiv on 26 November 2020 with entry date limits from December 2019 (please see search strategies in Appendix S1 of the Online Supplementary Document)
elements.reason: All databases/registers searched are named and the full search strategies are referenced in a supplementary appendix, but the complete search strings are not presented in the manuscript itself.

elements.quote: with entry date limits from December 2019 ... We included children (defined as ≤18 years old) who were attending school ... We excluded home-schooled children and their close contacts, and schools with student numbers below 20 ... We included articles in peer-reviewed journals and pre-prints, and excluded comments, conference abstracts and interviews.
elements.reason: Search limits (date limit from December 2019; publication type exclusions) are reported and eligibility criteria are described, but the limits are not explicitly justified by reference to the eligibility criteria.
No citation of published search approaches or filters, or description of adaptations, appears in the retrieved evidence.
No mention of natural-language processing or text-analysis tools for search term identification.
No mention of tools used to translate search strings between sources.
No description of validation of the search strategy.
No description of peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS).
Although a PECO approach is mentioned, no description of an alternative conceptual search structure or its development is provided.

elements.quote: We performed parallel review of titles, abstracts, and subsequently full texts based on updated inclusion and exclusion criteria following the population, exposure, comparison, outcome (PECO) approach
elements.reason: Parallel review implies multiple reviewers screened titles/abstracts and full texts, but the exact number of reviewers at each stage is not stated (numbers of reviewers are given only for data extraction and risk of bias).
The manuscript never explicitly states whether reviewers worked independently during title/abstract or full-text screening; 'parallel review' does not establish independence.
No description of how screening disagreements were resolved is provided in the retrieved evidence.
No evidence indicates that authors sought or needed additional eligibility information from study investigators; the conditional requirement does not appear to apply.
No mention of non-English articles or translation needs; the conditional requirement does not apply based on the evidence.
No automation tools are reported as being used in the selection process.
No externally derived classifiers are reported in the evidence.
No internally derived classifiers are reported in the evidence.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools or stopping rules are reported in the evidence.
No crowdsourcing platforms are reported in the evidence.
No previously screened datasets used to eliminate records are described in the evidence.

elements.quote: Data relevant to the evidence for SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools were extracted independently by two reviewers (WX, YD).
elements.reason: The Data Extraction section explicitly states that two reviewers extracted data from each report.

elements.quote: Data relevant to the evidence for SARS-CoV-2 transmission in schools were extracted independently by two reviewers (WX, YD).
elements.reason: The text states the two reviewers worked independently during data extraction.
No retrieved evidence describes how disagreements between data collectors were resolved during data extraction.
No retrieved evidence describes any process for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators.
No automation tools for data collection are described in the retrieved evidence.
No methods for translating articles for data collection are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No software for extracting data from figures is mentioned in the retrieved evidence.
No decision rules for selecting data from multiple reports or resolving inconsistencies between reports are described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: number of index cases, number of contacts, number of secondary infected cases, IAR: No. of secondary infected cases/ No. of contacts, number of participants tested for SARS-CoV-2, number of SARS-CoV-2 positive cases, and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rates: No. of positive cases/ No. of participants tested.
elements.reason: Outcome-related data items (IAR and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rates) are listed with brief operational definitions (ratios), but outcome domains are not formally listed and defined as outcome domains per se; they appear within a general data extraction list.
No time frame of measurement (e.g. follow-up duration for outcomes) is specified for the outcome domains in the retrieved evidence; only study-level investigation periods are reported.
The manuscript does not state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain (all measures, time points, analyses) were sought.
Conditional element; the manuscript does not indicate that only a subset of compatible results was sought, so no selection process needed to be described.
No evidence of changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance; the protocol update (text_3, text_4) concerned study-type inclusion criteria, not outcome domains.
No evidence of changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains; the reported protocol update related to study design inclusion criteria.
The manuscript does not report which outcomes were considered most important for interpreting conclusions or a rationale for prioritising them, although IAR is the meta-analysed outcome.

elements.quote: Data included: citation details, publication type, study design, country, region, city, investigation period, background population setting (country/regional COVID-19 prevalence rates), types of ... non-pharmaceutical intervention in the background population setting, school closures at the time of the study, number of schools included, type of schools, size of schools, types of non-pharmaceutical interventions in place in schools, sampling method ... provider testing vs self-testing, testing method ... modality of follow-up, frequency of follow-up, case and contact demographics (age and gender), clinical characteristics, number of index cases, number of contacts, number of secondary infected cases, IAR: No. of secondary infected cases/ No. of contacts ...
elements.reason: The Data Extraction section provides a comprehensive list of all variables sought, with definitions for derived outcomes (IAR, positivity rates).

No text describes assumptions made about missing or unclear study information. Tables use 'NA' entries but no explanation of how missing/unclear data were handled is provided in the retrieved evidence.

No tool (e.g., a data collection template or standardized form) used to determine which data items to collect is cited anywhere in the retrieved evidence; the conditional requirement is not fulfilled or demonstrably inapplicable.

elements.quote: evaluated the risk of bias in the included studies using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale (NOS) for controlled cohort and cross-sectional studies modified to reflect the school setting [11]
elements.reason: The tool (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale) is explicitly named, including that it was modified for the school setting.

elements.quote: The tools included an assessment of selection, measurement and attrition bias, and comparability
elements.reason: The domains assessed by the tool are specified (selection, measurement/detection, attrition bias, comparability), further detailed in Tables 6 and 7.

elements.quote: Ten studies were at high risk of detection bias caused by differences in screening or testing or both, and 9 of 11 studies were at high risk of attrition bias
elements.reason: Domain-level and summary judgements are reported (e.g., 'risk of bias was found to be high for most studies'), but explicit rules for deriving an overall risk-of-bias judgement are not described.

elements.quote: using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale (NOS) for controlled cohort and cross-sectional studies modified to reflect the school setting [11] and informed by earlier work [12]
elements.reason: Adaptation of the NOS to the school setting is described, and the modified tool is made available in supplementary materials.
No newly developed tool was used; an existing tool (modified NOS) was applied, so this element does not apply.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers (NS, CM) evaluated the risk of bias in the included studies
elements.reason: Number of reviewers (two), named reviewers, and independence are reported; however, no disagreement-resolution procedure is described, so this is arguably partial. Given independence and number are clearly stated, scored PRESENT with minor caveat.
No evidence that risk-of-bias information was sought or confirmed from study investigators; the requirement does not apply based on reported methods.
No automation tools were used for risk-of-bias assessment; assessment was performed manually by two reviewers.

elements.quote: We pooled SARS-CoV-2 infection attack rates (IAR) or positivity rates using a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird) [7]. To account for zero cell counts, we transformed raw numbers/proportions with the Freeman-Tukey double arcine method to stabilize the variance [8].
elements.reason: The synthesis measure is specified as pooled proportions (IAR/positivity rates, presented as percentages with 95% CIs, e.g. text_2 and table_5), covering the meta-analysed outcomes. However, no effect measure is specified for comparative outcomes (e.g. the cross-sectional study comparing school vs community positivity, or school vs community comparisons), so specification is not complete for every outcome type.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes, nor their rationale, are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

No methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure are described; only the Freeman-Tukey variance-stabilizing transformation is mentioned (text_6), which is not a re-expression into a different effect measure.
The choice of effect measure (pooled IAR/positivity proportions) is not justified or explained in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: We found 11 cohort studies [13-17,24-29] that investigated secondary infection attack (Table 1 and Table 2) and one cross-sectional studies [18] that investigated SARS-CoV-2 positivity compared to community rates (Table 3 and Table 4). Five cross-sectional studies [19-23] from our 1st update that investigated SARS-COV-2 positivity but did not compare with community rates were excluded.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the process for deciding study eligibility for each synthesis: studies were screened against updated inclusion/exclusion criteria based on a PECO approach (text_4), and were assigned to syntheses by design and outcome — cohort studies for secondary attack rates and cross-sectional studies only if they compared school positivity with community rates, with five cross-sectional studies excluded for lacking community comparison. The flowchart (figure_3, text_8) further shows how studies were allocated to narrative synthesis and meta-analysis by design.

elements.quote: To account for zero cell counts, we transformed raw numbers/proportions with the Freeman-Tukey double arcine method to stabilize the variance [8].
elements.reason: The manuscript describes data preparation for synthesis: derived calculations (IAR = No. of secondary infected cases/No. of contacts; positivity rates = No. of positive cases/No. of participants tested, per text_5) and a data transformation (Freeman-Tukey double arcine) to handle zero cell counts before pooling (text_6). Handling of other missing summary statistics is not explicitly described, but the core data preparation/conversion methods are reported.

elements.quote: the characteristics of the included studies are presented in Tables 1-4 . We found 11 cohort studies [13-17,24-29] that investigated secondary infection attack ( Table 1 and Table 2 ) and one cross-sectional studies [18] that investigated SARS-CoV-2 positivity compared to community rates ( Table 3 and Table 4 ).
elements.reason: Tables 1-5 are referenced and their content (study characteristics, IAR data) is evident from the tables themselves, but the Methods section does not describe the tabular structures or how data were tabulated for display.

elements.quote: Funnel plots and the Egger test were used to detect evidence of publication bias [10].
elements.reason: Funnel plots and Egger plots are mentioned in the Methods (for publication bias) and forest/funnel/Egger plots appear in Results (Figures 2-4), but the Methods section does not explicitly describe the graphical methods used to display results of individual studies and syntheses.
No evidence describes the basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or figures; tables are grouped by study design/update but this is not stated as a reporting method.
Only standard graphs (forest plots, funnel plots, Egger plots) are used; no non-standard graphs are reported, so no rationale is required.
